report.summary: Three findings: the new unauthenticated /api/export endpoint dumps the entire readings history as CSV and is not represented anywhere in the threat model (highest priority), plus a stale input-validation control claim and a missing DFD flow.

findings.title: New unauthenticated /api/export endpoint bulk-exports the whole readings database

model_excerpt.quote: GROWUD_BIND / -bind allows binding the dashboard to 0.0.0.0. The dashboard has no authentication, no CSRF protection, and no rate limiting. Anyone reachable on the network can read live energy data via /api/summary, query historical readings via /api/readings, retrieve computed grid import cost / export credit via /api/cost ...

evidence.note: New route registered: mux.HandleFunc("/api/export", s.handleAPIExport) — no auth middleware on the mux
handleAPIExport streams every stored reading as CSV; with no ?device= it exports all devices
ExportAllReadings returns every row in the readings table (no date bounding or row limit)

relevance.justification: The threat that enumerates the unauthenticated read surface omits a new endpoint that exfiltrates the entire energy-readings-db in one request.

findings.agent_prompt: Update growud.tm.hcl: the threat "Web dashboard bound to all interfaces exposes data and triggers Growatt API calls without authentication" (around line 127) enumerates /api/summary, /api/readings and /api/cost as the unauthenticated read surface. This PR added a new route /api/export (server/server.go: mux.HandleFunc("/api/export", s.handleAPIExport) and func handleAPIExport) backed by growatt/store.go ExportAllReadings, which streams the complete readings history for all devices as CSV with no authentication, no row limit and no date bounding. Extend that threat's description to include /api/export and note it is a full-database bulk export (highest-value target on the unauthenticated surface), keep information_asset "energy-readings-db" listed, and update the proposed control "Add an authentication layer (or refuse to bind non-loopback without it)" to explicitly cover /api/export (auth + rate limiting or row/date bounding).
findings.suggested_fix: Add /api/export to the unauthenticated-dashboard threat description and to the proposed auth/rate-limit control in growud.tm.hcl.

findings.title: 'Strict regex validation on date and device-SN inputs' no longer covers all query-parameter-driven endpoints

model_excerpt.quote: server.go validates date with ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$ and device with ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$, then time.Parse-checks the date. Applied uniformly to /api/readings and /api/cost (from/to/device). Store queries use parameterised SQL via database/sql, including QueryRangeReadings used by the cost calculator.

evidence.note: handleAPIExport reads r.URL.Query().Get("device") and passes it straight to the store without deviceSNRe.MatchString validation
ExportAllReadings interpolates no user data (uses ? placeholder), so SQL injection is not introduced, but the model's 'uniform validation' claim is now inaccurate

relevance.justification: The control is still true for the endpoints it names, but a new query-parameter-driven endpoint bypasses the validation the model presents as uniform.

findings.agent_prompt: Update growud.tm.hcl: the control "Strict regex validation on date and device-SN inputs" (implemented = true, around line 229) under the threat "Untrusted query parameters drive database / cost queries" claims validation is applied uniformly to the query-parameter endpoints. The new /api/export handler added in this PR (server/server.go handleAPIExport) reads the `device` query parameter and passes it to growatt/store.go ExportAllReadings without applying deviceSNRe. Either amend the control description to state that /api/export relies solely on parameterised SQL (no regex validation) and note the gap, or better, add deviceSNRe validation to handleAPIExport and update the description to list /api/export alongside /api/readings and /api/cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the input-validation control description in growud.tm.hcl to cover (or exclude) /api/export's unvalidated `device` parameter.

findings.title: DFD has no flow for the CSV export of energy-readings-db back to the user

model_excerpt.quote: flow "query readings": Web Dashboard (HTTP) -> SQLite DB (growud.db)

evidence.note: handleAPIExport writes a full CSV of all readings to the HTTP response (Content-Disposition attachment)
New store method ExportAllReadings supplies the bulk data set for the export flow

relevance.justification: A new bulk data egress path from the SQLite store through the dashboard to the requester is not represented in the DFD.

findings.agent_prompt: Update the data_flow_diagram_v2 "Growud" block in growud.tm.hcl (around line 255): add a flow representing the new bulk CSV export introduced in this PR — Web Dashboard (HTTP) -> SQLite DB (growud.db) named something like "export all readings" (backed by growatt/store.go ExportAllReadings) and a corresponding response flow Web Dashboard (HTTP) -> User named "CSV export (all readings)" carrying information_asset "energy-readings-db", so the DFD shows the full-history egress path added by server/server.go handleAPIExport.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "export all readings" and "CSV export" flows to the DFD in growud.tm.hcl covering energy-readings-db egress via /api/export.
